facility_roles.note: BaBar was built and operated at SLAC on the PEP-II collider.

facility_roles.locator: INSPIRE experiment record 1108553; CERN Courier, "BaBar celebrates its 25th anniversary"
facility_roles.note: The PEP-II asymmetric e⁺e⁻ beams that BaBar recorded were produced and accelerated at SLAC; PEP-II was built by SLAC, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

intervals.label: construction (inferred bound)
intervals.note: "Less than six years" is measured by the source from the end-of-1993 organizing meeting, not the 1996-01-31 formal approval used as this interval's start; the span is therefore an upper bound, not a tightly sourced construction period.
intervals.quote: Less than six years later, PEP-II and the BaBar detector were built and the first collision events were collected on 26 May 1999.

intervals.label: PEP-II/BaBar physics running
intervals.locator: CERN Courier, "BaBar celebrates its 25th anniversary" (2019); end date per Symmetry Magazine, "End of PEP-II and BaBar runs at SLAC" (2008-04-08)
intervals.note: Symmetry Magazine's own dateline is 2008-04-08, but its text says the beams were dumped and BaBar took its last data "last night" -- i.e. the calendar day of the last collisions could be 2008-04-07 by the time zone the article was written in, not the publication day itself. INSPIRE's date_completed for BaBar is month-precision only (2008-04), which does not resolve the day. Recorded here as the article's own dateline rather than an independently confirmed event day; verification review, 2026-09-17.
intervals.quote: the first collision events were collected on 26 May 1999

intervals.label: PEP-II shutdown; BaBar data-taking ends
intervals.locator: Symmetry Magazine, "End of PEP-II and BaBar runs at SLAC" (2008-04-08)
intervals.note: Symmetry Magazine's own dateline is 2008-04-08, but its text says the beams were dumped and BaBar took its last data "last night" -- i.e. the actual last-data day could be 2008-04-07, one day before the article's own dateline. INSPIRE's date_completed for BaBar is month-precision only (2008-04). Day given as the article's dateline, not an independently confirmed event day; verification review, 2026-09-17.
intervals.quote: Last night, the beams were dumped for the final time from the PEP-II rings and the BaBar experiment took its last data. It was the end of nine years of operation.

CERN Courier reports BaBar's organizational predecessor ("the Detector Collaboration for the PEP-II asymmetric electron-positron collider") held its inaugural meeting at SLAC at the end of 1993, and the collaboration adopted the name "BaBar" by May 1994 -- distinct from, and earlier than, the 1994-06 date_proposed field on the INSPIRE experiment record, which likely reflects the formal proposal submission rather than the informal organizing meeting.

physics_goals.quote: The primary aim is a detailed study of CP violating asymmetries in B0 meson decay, but a wide variety of other B, charm, tau, and two-photon physics will also be accessible.
physics_goals.value: Detailed study of CP-violating asymmetries in neutral B-meson decay, with a wide variety of other B, charm, tau and two-photon physics also accessible

summary.plain: A particle detector at SLAC, near Stanford, California, built to study why matter and antimatter behave slightly differently by watching B mesons decay. It ran from 1999 to 2008 and, together with Japan's Belle experiment, confirmed a theory that won the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physics.
summary.technical: General-purpose detector at the PEP-II asymmetric e⁺e⁻ B-factory (SLAC), operating at the Υ(4S) resonance (10.58 GeV) to study CP violation in neutral B-meson decays via the entangled B⁰-B̄⁰ pairs produced. First collisions 26 May 1999; data-taking ended 8 April 2008. Co-observed CP violation in the B⁰ system (2001) with Belle at KEK.

unique_capabilities.quote: The "asymmetric" descriptor of the collider refers to Pier Oddone's concept of using unequal electron and positron beam energies ... tuned to 10.58 GeV, the mass of the Υ(4S) meson.
unique_capabilities.value: An asymmetric-energy e⁺e⁻ collider tuned to the Υ(4S) resonance, giving the produced B and anti-B mesons a relativistic boost that lets their decay points be resolved -- essential for time-dependent CP-violation measurements
